ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the input Vi first passes through the left resistor R and is connected to the upper output node, and the output V0 is the voltage of this node relative to the bottom common reference line. The output node is connected downward to two diode clipping branches: the left branch is D1 in series connected to the reference power supply labeled -1 V, and the right branch is D2 in series connected to the reference power supply labeled +2 V. Reasoning: The forward conduction voltage drop of a silicon diode is 0.7 V. According to the direction of D1 in the figure, when the output node is another 0.7 V lower than the -1 V reference terminal, D1 begins to conduct, so the lower-limit clamping threshold is V0 = -1 - 0.7 = -1.7 V. According to the direction of D2 in the figure, when the output node is 0.7 V higher than the +2 V reference terminal, D2 begins to conduct, so the upper-limit clamping threshold is V0 = 2 + 0.7 = 2.7 V. If V0 = Vi is required, then both diodes must be cut off; at this time there is no current in resistor R, and there is no voltage drop across the resistor, so the output node voltage equals the input voltage. Thus Vi must be strictly between the two conduction thresholds.

raw_record.question_text: The circuit shown uses two silicon diodes, each with a forward voltage drop of 0.7 V. What is the range of input voltage \(V_i\) for which the output voltage satisfies \(V_0 = V_i\)?

method.method_draft: First identify the two limiting clamp voltages from the image. D1 is oriented so it turns on when the output node falls 0.7 V below the -1 V reference, giving the lower clamp threshold V0 = -1 - 0.7 = -1.7 V. D2 is oriented so it turns on when the output node rises 0.7 V above the +2 V reference, giving the upper clamp threshold V0 = 2 + 0.7 = 2.7 V. For V0 to equal Vi, both diodes must be off, leaving the resistor with zero current and therefore zero voltage drop. Thus require the output/input node to lie strictly between the two turn-on thresholds: -1.7 V < Vi < 2.7 V.

method.method_draft: Assume the desired operating region V0 = Vi. Then the voltage across R is zero, so the output node cannot be supplying current into either diode branch; both diodes must be nonconducting. Apply the off-bias inequalities using the polarities read from the image. For D1, anode voltage is -1 V and cathode voltage is V0, so off requires (-1) - V0 < 0.7, hence V0 > -1.7 V. For D2, anode voltage is V0 and cathode voltage is +2 V, so off requires V0 - 2 < 0.7, hence V0 < 2.7 V. Since in this assumed region V0 = Vi, combine the inequalities to get -1.7 V < Vi < 2.7 V. The endpoint cases are excluded because a diode is just at turn-on and the idealized equality region is taken as the both-off region.

图像描述：图中输入端 Vi 的正端经过电阻 R 接到右侧的输出上节点，输出电压 V0 是该上节点相对于下方公共参考线的电压。该输出节点向下有两条二极管支路：左支路为 D1 接到标注为 -1 V 的电压源上端，右支路为 D2 接到标注为 +2 V 的电压源上端。按图中二极管方向，D1 的阳极在 -1 V 端、阴极在 V0 节点；D2 的阳极在 V0 节点、阴极在 +2 V 端。
推理：假设要求的工作区间满足 V0 = Vi，则电阻 R 两端电压为零，因此输出节点不应向任何二极管支路供电流，两只二极管都必须处于截止状态。硅二极管导通条件为阳极电压比阴极电压高约 0.7 V。
对 D1，阳极电压为 -1 V，阴极电压为 V0。截止要求 (-1) - V0 < 0.7，因此 V0 > -1.7 V。
对 D2，阳极电压为 V0，阴极电压为 +2 V。截止要求 V0 - 2 < 0.7，因此 V0 < 2.7 V。
在该假设区间内 V0 = Vi，所以把 V0 换成 Vi，得到 -1.7 V < Vi < 2.7 V。端点处有二极管正好达到导通阈值，因此按两二极管均截止的等式区间排除端点。

claims.claim: According to the direction of D1 in the figure, when the output node is another 0.7 V lower than the -1 V reference terminal, D1 begins to conduct.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: According to the direction of D1 in the figure, when the output node is another 0.7 V lower than the -1 V reference terminal, D1 begins to conduct

claims.claim: The lower-limit clamping threshold of D1 is V0 = -1 - 0.7 = -1.7 V.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore the lower-limit clamping threshold is V0 = -1 - 0.7 = -1.7 V

claims.claim: According to the direction of D2 in the figure, when the output node is 0.7 V higher than the +2 V reference terminal, D2 begins to conduct.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: According to the direction of D2 in the figure, when the output node is 0.7 V higher than the +2 V reference terminal, D2 begins to conduct

claims.claim: The upper-limit clamping threshold of D2 is V0 = 2 + 0.7 = 2.7 V.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore the upper-limit clamping threshold is V0 = 2 + 0.7 = 2.7 V

claims.claim: If V0 = Vi is required, then both diodes must be cut off.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: If V0 = Vi is required, then both diodes must be cut off

claims.claim: When both diodes are cut off, there is no current in resistor R.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: At this time there is no current in resistor R

claims.claim: When both diodes are cut off, there is no voltage drop across the resistor.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: There is no voltage drop across the resistor

claims.claim: When both diodes are cut off, the output node voltage equals the input voltage.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: So the output node voltage equals the input voltage

claims.claim: Vi must be strictly between the two conduction thresholds of -1.7 V and 2.7 V.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Thus Vi must be strictly between the two conduction thresholds
